subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-class per-model memory indexes for safe embedding failover now, and should that live in bundled memory-core, a plugin API extension, or an external memory plugin?
rationale: The request is not a narrow bug fix; it adds new config surface, persistent data-model changes, ingestion coordination, provider-routing policy, status semantics, and migration/doctor requirements that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design memory-core/API contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open and have the memory owner define the config, storage, migration, status, and plugin-boundary contract before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin/API extension
options.body: If maintainers want this outside bundled memory-core, define the missing plugin seam and let an external memory plugin own multi-index failover.

options.title: Defer broad failover
options.body: Keep the existing identity guard and only fix narrower provider recovery bugs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534 for now.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core/API contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and have the memory owner define the config, storage, migration, status, and plugin-boundary contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is assigned on the live issue and has recent commits in the provider fallback, local embedding, and index identity area this decision depends on.
